Key Research Thinking Patterns: Multimodal Radiomic Prognostication: Integrating high-dimensional imaging features with clinical scales to predict patient outcomes (e.g., using Haralick Textural Attributes and PCA on MRI T2/FLAIR sequences to predict Acute Ischemic Stroke functional outcomes via ASPECTS scoring).

Explainable AI for Trustworthy NLP: Leveraging large language models and semantic modeling to detect misinformation and enhance public policy transparency (e.g., fine-tuning RoBERTa/BERT with Regression-based Trustworthiness Scoring and TRUExT tool for news media analysis).

Physics-Informed Material Property Prediction: Combining microstructural image analysis with mechanical testing data to screen unconventional resources (e.g., using SEM images and Nanoindentation data with Random Forests to predict shale elastic properties).

Human-in-the-Loop Visual Analytics: Designing interactive systems that fuse real-time data streams with user feedback for situational awareness (e.g., employing Interactive Machine Learning and Ensemble Visualization in SMART 2.0 to track misinformation during the UK 2024 Riots).
Summary Description: David Ebert is an interdisciplinary data scientist specializing in explainable AI, visual analytics, and computational modeling across healthcare, geoenergy, and national security. He develops robust prognostic frameworks for acute ischemic stroke using radiomic feature extraction and clinical scales, while simultaneously advancing unconventional resource exploration through physics-informed machine learning of shale properties. His work in computational social science pioneers real-time misinformation detection and crisis response systems, utilizing large language models and human-in-the-loop interactive visualization. By bridging medical imaging, petrophysics, and natural language processing, Ebert creates scalable, quantitative decision-support tools that enhance trust, safety, and operational efficiency in high-stakes societal challenges.
